Watisoni Waqanisaravi extends La Rochelle contract till 2028

item.content:encoded:
Former Kaiviti Silktails prop Watisoni Waqanisaravi has secured a contract extension with French Top 14 club La Rochelle after his planned loan move to Nevers was called off.

Waqanisaravi , who can play at lock and in the back row, was recalled by Ronan O'Gara's coaching staff following a number of injuries in the second row, including to Will Skelton and Salmaan Moerat.

Since then, Waqanisaravi has made three Top 14 appearances, compared with just four league appearances last season.

The former Lelean Memorial School student, who stands 1.95 metres tall and weighs 127kg, has showcased his power since the resumption of the league.

Waqanisaravi says he is delighted to have extended his stay with La Rochelle and is looking forward to continuing his development at the French club.

He thanked the coaching staff for their confidence in him and the fans for their continued support as he looks to make the most of his opportunities this season.

item.title: Bituniyata named ProD2 Player of the Season
item.description: Fiji international Setareki Bituniyata has been named the ProD2 Player of the Season after playing a key role in helping Provence qualify for the competition’s final. The Nadroga-born forward with maternal links to Tailevu, has been recognised for his performances throughout the season as Provence pushed for promotion.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji international Setareki Bituniyata has been named the ProD2 Player of the Season after playing a key role in helping Provence qualify for the competition’s final.

The Nadroga-born forward with maternal links to Tailevu, has been recognised for his performances throughout the season as Provence pushed for promotion.

Bituniyata's latest achievement adds to an impressive year for the Fijian, who has also earned selection in the 68-member FIJI Water Flying Fijians squad for their upcoming Test against Japan and the Northern Tour.

Fiji will face Japan at 5.50pm on Saturday, October 24.

The Flying Fijians will then begin their November campaign against France on 8 November 8, followed by a Test against Ireland on November 15.

Fiji will conclude the Northern Tour against Italy on November 22.

item.title: Manchester City found guilty of serious financial breaches
item.description: Manchester City has been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over nine seasons and could face fines, points deductions or other sporting sanctions. An independent Commission found City guilty of all serious financial charges covering the 2009/10 to 2017/18 seasons and most charges relating to its failure to co-operate with the Premier League investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Manchester City has been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over nine seasons and could face fines, points deductions or other sporting sanctions.

An independent Commission found City guilty of all serious financial charges covering the 2009/10 to 2017/18 seasons and most charges relating to its failure to co-operate with the Premier League investigation.

The Commission found the club used sham commercial deals to artificially increase revenue and reduce costs by more than £900 million, equivalent to about FJ$2.68 billion, to appear to comply with financial rules.

It also found City filed misstated accounts, concealed the true state of its finances and significantly breached Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

Premier League Chief Executive Richard Masters has described it as the most significant disciplinary case in Premier League history.

No punishment has been announced, with sanctions to be decided at a separate hearing.

Manchester City has until Friday to appeal the findings.
